confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from web searches of crowdsourced cost-of-living data. MyLifeElsewhere lists an inexpensive meal with a drink at about USD 7.46, a cappuccino at about USD 2.03 and a pint of domestic beer at about USD 2.42. A Numbeo Florianópolis page lists a mid-range three-course meal for two, without drinks, at about BRL 235, but the page is undated. I converted BRL to USD at an assumed rate of about 5.4, which I did not check. I raised the figures slightly for inflation by July 2026. I treated beer as a draft chopp of about BRL 12–15. Cocktails are less certain: a local guide gives BRL 30–50 for signature cocktails, and a beach-kiosk caipirinha costs about BRL 40. I used a typical bar caipirinha of about BRL 35. I found no direct price for a glass of wine, so I estimated it from the beer and cocktail prices and typical Brazilian wine markups of about BRL 28–32. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or listings. July is the winter low season in Florianópolis, so prices are below the December–February summer peak. Prices also vary a lot by area: Jurerê Internacional and Lagoa da Conceição cost more than Centro.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are set slightly above Brazil's national average and close to other affluent coastal or southern Brazilian cities such as Porto Alegre and Curitiba, but below premium areas of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. Crowdsourced data puts Florianópolis restaurant prices about 15% above the Brazilian average.
